scope: RETAINED NEGATIVE establishing a boundary, not a pad-level verdict: reaching a pad's IOMUX terminal in the routed netlist with a valid feeder is NOT sufficient for that pad to drive on silicon. The one qualified top-edge pad (PIN_18) additionally has a characterized pad APPROACH -- a pinned driver site plus a forced approach chain plus the matching iomux_hop_vendor row for that exact feeder -- and iomux_hop_vendor.csv contains rows for only two pads. No claim is made that the other eight pads cannot drive; they are untested pending the harvested approach. Also NOT claimed: any widening of the qualified output set, which remains the left-edge PIN_25-PIN_28 plus characterized header outputs.

observed: Decoded all 66 pad approach chains from the vendor build that routes all 33 L48 pads simultaneously (padmap_full_20260814/logic_db/route.tx) and compared, per top-edge pad, the feeder RMUX that agamemnon/chipdb/padfeed_L48_top.csv offers against the feeder the vendor actually drives into that pad's IOMUX. The nine disagreements are PIN_19 ours RMUX8 vs vendor RMUX16; PIN_17 RMUX20 vs RMUX16; PIN_16 {RMUX0,4,8,16,24} vs RMUX12; PIN_15 RMUX16 vs RMUX28; PIN_14 RMUX0 vs RMUX24; PIN_13 RMUX12 vs RMUX8; PIN_10 RMUX24 vs RMUX8; PIN_11 RMUX28 vs RMUX4; PIN_12 RMUX20 vs RMUX0.
scope: Data defect located in padfeed_L48_top.csv, explaining a standing silicon observation rather than adding a claim. PIN_18 -- the single top-edge pad that has ever driven on silicon -- is the single pad whose shipped feeder matches the vendor's. The other nine route to their IOMUX terminal and configure, but drive nothing, consistent with our table pointing the router at a different physical approach than the silicon uses. This does NOT establish that the nine pads will work once corrected; it identifies the correction to make and the prediction to test. No feature claim changes.
